reviews.text: ...a stirring action picture that grows more and more absorbing as it unfolds...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: A riveting war story that reveals the bonds that build between soldiers and interpreters
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: In telling a specific story of wartime camaraderie, the film offers good fodder for discussions of grace, guilt, and the gospel.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: It is a tight drama that looks at the war in Afghanistan in 2018 and its aftermath that works on multiple levels and is so finely written that it flows from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: In a film that is supposed to focus on the tragedy of Afghan civilians during and after the war, it is at least disconcerting that the point of view is that of Sergeant Kinley... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Natalia Trzenko

reviews.text: I am really frustrated by this one even as a massive fan of Guy Ritchies...
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The Covenant keeps the attention on the bond and relationship between the two men, and portrays it as a show of humanity amidst the barbaric. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: With the men's dynamic and their few words, The Covenant could've been a Western (and in a certain way it is). [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: The Covenant is also known under its official title Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant, although I suppose a more accurate moniker might be Guy Ritchie’s The Killing Fields.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Ritchie did not have to put his name in the title of the strongest, most impressive film of his career. It’s a defining showcase that liberates him from his genre. It is Gyllenhaal’s most assured role. A highly realistic war film.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: ... uses the real-world experiences of many as inspiration for a dramatic wartime tale in which the bonds forged in battle cannot be undone, no matter time and distance.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is good as the intense American sergeant...
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: The Covenant is a disciplined and effective war movie with a real point to make about the civilian workers who were left behind.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: …as entertaining and exciting as it is thought provoking.
reviews.author: Erin Free

reviews.text: [Gyllenhaal 's] energy is perfect for the relatively sober-minded The Covenant — and allows space for Dar Salim to shine, in a more substantial lead than the majority of his Hollywood roles have afforded him so far.
reviews.author: Catherine Bray

reviews.text: …the film’s second half, largely focused Killing Fields-style on Kinney’s attempts to rescue Ahmed, is the exact opposite of the casual betrayal which took place in real life…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Though the movie is fictional, the uncertain fate of thousands of real Afghan interpreters after the hurried 2021 US withdrawal gives it genuine heft.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's strategically shameful action thriller points an accusatory finger at broken covenants (promises) made to loyal Afghan interpreters/translators by the U.S. Government, leaving them stranded as prime targets for Taliban reprisals.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: These set pieces are extraordinarily well done, brutal, and eye-opening to everyday dangers. Still, the final act would have worked better if it dealt with Ahmed's struggle to survive rather than Kinley's guilt and depression.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The serious melodrama falters when it becomes little more than an action movie devoid of the melodrama.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: A searing war drama with considerable edge-of-your-seat moments.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: This feels like a breath of fresh air [for Guy Ritchie]. He is really reinvigorated by paring it down.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Like two films in one, this “Covenant” doesn’t seem like other examples, even though Ritchie embraces plenty of clichés. It works because the actors commit to the missions.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: The reunion brought tears to my eyes--Guy Ritchie’s seasoned filmmaking career has created an excellent film of friendship, devotion, and the realistic horrors of war.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Director Guy Ritchie dispenses with his usual fancy flourishes and keeps the action straight-forward...He ratchets up the tension as the urgency mounts in a cut-to-the-chase scenario that gives a sense of real-time heroics.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: It's essentially a male-bonding story about two unlikely comrades saving each other's asses, and the screenplay does its due diligence by addressing the psychological trauma they endure.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A capably made but simple-minded rescue film, one with a big heart — even if it could have used more brain.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Ritchie surprises with a much more conventional action movie. Dar Salim is excellent in this stripped-back soldier story that is more poignant than the trailers suggested.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: In theory it is all there - the acting, the story, the direction - but it never seems to completely come together.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Like just about every Guy Ritchie work, Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant isn’t all it could have been. It deserves to be seen, though, and, at least for a while, remembered.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: The perfect two person story.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: The intensity of the men's predicament might have been better served by Peter Berg or Paul Greengrass, both of whose frenetic styles more aptly fit the material.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: The action scenes are well-staged, and there is plenty of suspense in the rescue scenes, too. Gyllenhaal, one of the best actors of his generation, shines in this role. He plays a man more haunted than idealistic.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: This gripping look at war gets under your skin.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: That Salim and Gyllenhaal are so good almost seems like an afterthought because Ritchie has us too involved in their characters' plight to get distracted by the artifice.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: A deadly serious—and almost deadly earnest, in its portrait of duty, honor, and sacrifice—look at America’s failure to live up to its word to the interpreters on the ground in Afghanistan.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: It’s Gyllenhaal and Salim that make the movie leave a dent in the viewer long after the credits conclude. As men cut from a more similar cloth than either would like to admit-they’re both family men serving in a war-they make the quieter moments count.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It is as always important to reassure Americans that we at least mean well with our pointless destructive wars, not like “bad” countries... A person predisposed to believe that might find The Covenant enjoyable. I did not.
reviews.author: William Schwartz

reviews.text: This is Ritchie at his most sedate and naturalistic, which makes sense in the context of this story.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The Covenant doesn’t arouse the stirrings of fervor that many war movies tap into but neither is it a nihilistic descent into the inhumanity of battle.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: "A taut military thriller with two fantastic performances, Guy Ritchie's The Covenant brings to mind the Afghans we left behind."
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: Swinging back to a more serious register, Ritchie presents his first film grounded in harsh real-world politics, and it’s the best film he’s made in years.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Through the Herculean efforts of Jake Gyllenhaal and Dar Salim, Guy Ritchie’s THE COVENANT is a gripping film exposing the horrors of the Afghanistan War.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie’s THE COVENANT is two hours of pure adrenaline as we wait for this remarkable story to unfold. It's a highly emotional journey that is impossible to dismiss.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: A dour lecture punctuated by some rousing action sequences.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: The Covenant is a solid story of survival, respect, and honor, while still acknowledging the brutality and senselessness of war. It’s easy to get caught up in this journey, and one of Ritchie’s better recent efforts.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The director, coming off a run of successful action comedies, shifts into a moving but flawed tale of friendship in the war in Afghanistan.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: The Covenant is nowhere near the ultimate cinematic statement on what happened in Afghanistan, but it is a riveting story worth telling from that battlefield.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: What we get is not only his most restrained and most focused movie in years. I think it’s Ritchie’s best movie in years period.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: What gives “Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant” its solid footing is the twinned performances by Gyllanhaal and Salim.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's The Covenant offers an overly simplistic portrayal of an American rescue mission in Afghanistan. However, this action flick has solid performances and capably shows the importance of interpreters during war.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: An uncharacteristically serious movie by director Guy Ritchie, this war-themed tale is simplistic but sturdy and effective thanks to crisp, energetic filmmaking and a touching emotional core.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The least Guy Ritchie film Guy Ritchie has yet made boasts a title bearing his name. Even as Ritchie quiets his quirks, there's still considerable style and scope here. Melancholy, mournful and meaty dramatic filmmaking that's less rah-rah, more requiem.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Harmful stuff comes with such nasty work, but so does the loyalty, friendship, and mutual respect that filmmaker Ritchie dramatizes just about perfectly after collecting these incidents for the big screen.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal stars in skillfully made and gripping film...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The Covenant is a well crafted, action packed and intense drama expertly directed by Guy Ritchie featuring career best acting work from Jake Gyllenhaal and Dar Salim. A film about the bonds of brotherhood that'll move you, enlighten you and uplift you!
reviews.author: John Rocha

reviews.text: If you think Guy Ritchie's The Covenant is simply just another movie about war, you are in for a large and pleasant surprise.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: For much of its running time, director Ritchie’s war movie manages to be topical, suspenseful, and moving. But partly because the story is fiction, Ritchie takes a few genre liberties that threaten to undermine the sincerity of his tale.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Much like Ritchie’s last feature, Mission:Impossible-wannabe Operation Fortune, The Covenant is completely devoid of any of the stylistic tics that once marked the director’s work.
reviews.author: Steven Warner

reviews.text: The Covenant does merit bonus points for showcasing Salim, a terrific journeyman actor who finally has a meaty role in an American movie.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Ritchie pulls off the best film of his career in nearly 20 years thanks to Jake Gyllenhaal and his own no-fuss, no-muss approach to mean-and-lean filmmaking and storytelling.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: This is not a true story. The truth is a disgrace. A throwback to those Chuck Norris "Missing in Action" films.  Gyllenhaal and Salim are fine. But this film is a fraud.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Contains some of the most poetic imagery that Ritchie’s ever filmed
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: While the battle scenes are effective and visceral, I yearned for the dialogue to have a little more of the color and life that Ritchie’s known for. Most of the movie sounds like someone entered “Write a war movie” into ChatGPT.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: This is a tense war drama, given more gravitas from the stellar performances of Gyllenhaal and Salim. As it goes along, it becomes a metaphor for the long slog that the U.S. got themselves into, as the “longest war” just ended recently. Good for? NOTHING!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: It’s a more than welcome break from Ritchie’s usual in-your-face style and suggests that Ritchie, just months away from turning 55, has finally matured as a filmmaker.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: A muscular, overwrought war film.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie is only one of a handful of directors known for a signature style. But he abandons it in "The Covenant," a pretty straightforward but solidly executed war story.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: ... resonates most powerfully by finding a fresh perspective on familiar themes of brotherhood and loyalty along the front lines.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: A sober military thriller that excoriates Joe Biden’s decision to pull out of Afghanistan in 2021 and, in the process, to strand the thousands of local interpreters who had risked their lives to aid the American cause.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: It’s a dramatically effective action thriller, but “The Covenant” is also an uncomfortably jingoistic combat movie.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: A serious military drama about valor, courage, honor, and the profound devotion of military personnel who serve alongside one another in times of war. Hope to see more spec ops military movies from director Guy Ritchie.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: How does it honor these brave and essential people to make a movie that isn’t about any of them but rather a near-superhuman fictional character?
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: It’s good to see Ritchie branch out — just like after “Snatch” and “The Man From U.N.C.L.E.,” he made us all do a double-take with “Aladdin.” Not everything works in “The Covenant,” but he’s not lost in the desert, either.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: For all its clichés, this furious and discomfiting film tugs on your conscience for days, making a powerful case to turn the American public’s attention back to a conflict it would rather forget.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: The Covenant works best when the two leads are forced to be silent lest they tip off prowling combatants.
reviews.author: Dex Wesley Parra

reviews.text: Hardly a revisionist film, either in terms of war movies in general or those about Afghanistan in particular; but as a tale of unlikely wartime comradeship, it’s a strong, compelling piece.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Though possibly well-intentioned, the execution of The Covenant ensures its narrative and thematic potential is drowned out in the roar of gunfire it becomes far too enamored by.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's film cuts through the complications ... to get at something so unquestionable that it is essentially an unmistakable, universal truth.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant delivers the action and suspense expected from the war movie genre and from Ritchie, yet ventures beyond expectations to create a moving drama.
reviews.author: Ayelet Dekel

reviews.text: An oftentimes riveting war film which marks a new path for the 54-year-old filmmaker.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: It’s unclear where this side of Guy Ritchie has been hiding all these years, but the juxtaposition of his regular fare to the well-done drama in The Covenant makes you wonder what else he might be able to do.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal and Dar Salim are superb in a visceral display of brotherhood on the battlefield. Guy Ritchie's The Covenant leaves no man behind.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal, who’s looking more and more like a trimmer Javier Bardem, uses that handsome-hangdog face of his to good effect. Salim, an Iraqi-born Danish actor, is very good. If he weren’t, the movie simply wouldn’t work.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Instead of layering on jump cuts, crazy camera angles and jokey subtitles like he usually does, he keeps things calm. Ritchie lets the action unfold swiftly and clearly.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The result is one of Ritchie’s finest films that’s made all the better by two extraordinary performances.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: An absorbing, action-driven war movie with great performances form Jake Gyllenhaal and Dar Salim.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The most suspenseful and heartfelt movie in Guy Ritchie's career.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: It about as exciting, gripping and moving as war films get -- especially one set in the murky Afghanistan conflict in which the U.S. found itself immersed for more than two decades.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Director Guy Ritchie exercises considerable restraint in his depiction of action: again and again, he is content to pull back, hold the shot, and let what happens be enough to engage the viewer. And again and again, it's more than enough.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: A masterfully manipulative war thriller...
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It's Guy Ritchie’s strongest film in quite some time. He feels at home with the genre and the focus needed to help the audience re-examine whatever feeling they have about the war in Afghanistan.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Offers marginal entertainment value. It’s a film that seems afraid to offer any ideas about its setting and characters beyond the minimum.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: Here, working from such familiar modern-warfare sentiment, Guy Ritchie's flash-bang technique becomes just another Hollywood grunt.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant is as sharp on deep human elements as it is with intensity, giving rise to a welcomed change in the director’s repertoire.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: The Covenant is more than just a great action movie, it’s a movie with purpose.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's The Covenant is a pulse-pounding and visceral look At keeping a promise, with Jake Gyllenhaal compelling as ever.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The acting by Gyllenhaal and Dar Sajim, who plays Ahmed, is outstanding and I think no matter your political persuasion you’ll be rooting for these 2 men to save each other.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Ritchie delivers his most mature film yet.  Without relying on his usual bag of tricks he delivers a thrilling and entertaining movie about the lengths two men will go to to do the right thing.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: Outside of universal themes involving friendship, bonding, and bravery, I can’t say the Brit filmmaker is doing much to enlighten me on how he feels about the politics of it all, but his efforts to deliver a strong feature pay off.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Directed by Ritchie with breathless, propulsive momentum, "The Covenant" is really about two wars. There's the one in the battlefield and the other one at home when some soldiers went to great lengths to bring their abandoned interpreters to the U.S.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: “The Covenant” unveils something new: Ritchie the contempo classicist. We’re seeing a born-again filmmaker.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: The movie’s full title, “Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant,” suggests either a marketing department run amok or a director having a full-blown ego trip, or both. But to Ritchie’s credit, he’s made a movie to be proud of.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A gritty change of pace for the director.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Suspense is big here, with Ritchie blending wartime pressure points with explosive moments of frustration, backed by a production team that’s dedicated to making a propulsive viewing experience.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie’s The Covenant is one of his best films, unlike anything the director has ever made. Jake Gyllenhaal and Dar Salim are riveting, effectively developing their bond and holding this emotionally draining story up in each of their own valiant ways
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: While one may want a greater depth or improved structural balance towards that end, there’s virtue to a story with simple, clear-cut goals.
reviews.author: Jeff Ewing

reviews.text: A deeply meaningful and touching story of honor and brotherhood that’s wrapped up in an intense wartime thriller.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: For Ritchie, war is quite grand, and a great way for dudes to get to know each other.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: The Covenant isn’t Guy Ritchie’s best, but standout performances from Jake Gyllenhaal and Dar Salim as bonded heroes save an otherwise bloated military thriller.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Remains firmly Ritchie’s stylistic wheelhouse... while proving to be intense and effective as a straightforward war drama. It might even lead one to ask why hasn’t been making “serious” cinema this whole time.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The Covenant resonates with an emphatic punch.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: In its best moments, The Covenant plays like an anti-war genre picture from the late ’70s and early ’80s. Political in spurts, intense throughout, and incredibly well-performed, Ritchie’s film moves faster than most modern studio fare.
reviews.author: Dan Mecca

reviews.text: This is Guy Ritchie’s best movie in quite some time, maybe because he handles the subject matter as seriously as it deserves to be handled.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Some frustrating pacing issues, distracting use of text on screen & a questionable message hold the film back, but the action is kinetic & looks fantastic, and the two central performances are deeply emotionally compelling. Solid overall war picture.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: The film bangs the drum loudly on behalf of American exceptionalism.
reviews.author: Greg Nussen

reviews.text: Ritchie’s abilities can craft some engrossing sequences that texture the storytelling nicely, with also a shout-out to the alluring score, but most of the time, he’s somewhat reserved.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: The overwhelmingly jingoistic, oorah approach certainly doesn’t match up with the critical gaze you might expect from a handful of Brits making a movie about one of America’s most sketchily motivated wars in a history of sketchily motivated wars.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

synopsis: Guy Ritchie's The Covenant follows US Army Sergeant John Kinley (Jake Gyllenhaal) and Afghan interpreter Ahmed (Dar Salim). After an ambush, Ahmed goes to Herculean lengths to save Kinley’s life. When Kinley learns that Ahmed and his family were not given safe passage to America as promised, he must repay his debt by returning to the war zone to retrieve them before the Taliban hunts them down first.
